title: We are heading towards an era where consumers can generate their own dream games without a middle-man AI game developer.
author: XalAtoh
selftext:
It is just a matter of time till ChatGpt, Gemini, Claude will have a dedicated "Game studio" mode, where the average joe can just type in their dream game and it will generate that game.

Especially when AI companies "learns" consumer's habits and interest.

Building a game gets easier and easier, eventually we won't need middle-man anymore.

I e.g. don't need a 3rd party gamestudio or solo-developer asking AI to generate a game for me, I can do this for myself.

MMO games are harder to generate, but even that will be solved as AI tech improves... eventually AI could replicate believable living MMO environment in an offline mode.

comments.author: DrinkTeaFightMonster
comments.body:
Every time a technology appears to lower barriers, we think everyone will design their own things.

Supply will increase, yes, but the whole thing only works because most people are consumers. Maybe they like consuming, maybe they don't have time to create and sometimes they have nothing they want to create.. but if everyone created, who would consume?

What it does do is increase supply and lead to innovation. Mobile games created whole new genres that were not present in console and PC. 

The most possibly exciting thing here is creators from small remote communities. Let's say, someone who comes from a community where they speak a unique language and the population isn't large enough to sustain a game dev team. E.g. Malta - 550,000 people and they speak Maltese. 

So today a Maltese who wants to make a bigger game has to join a team in continental Europe or in one of the bigger countries. They have to physically move, learn a new language etc.

What if this person had AI? They can now create.. out of their living room. 

And more.. what about physically disabled persons? It's challenging for them to join game teams, but what if they had something to say and they were amazing creators?

comments.author: PoorSquirrrel

Nah.

There's a lot more that goes into a game that none of the current AI models will be able to do in the forseable future. We can't even explain it in words most of the time. Why some games just work and another very similar game doesn't.

There's a sector of games, cookie-cutter formulaic titles. From cheap mobile knock-offs to AAA games that decided to not take any risk. AI can do much of that, but it can't decide if the game is fun. There's no metric for "fun". The "feel" of a game is a balance of so many different factors and even if you get all of them right, they might not work together in that combination.

What we see these days on social media is stuff that I am very sure would fall apart under in a solid QA testing, and is essentially fan-fiction. That's a good comparison, I think. We have writing as a tool for the masses for quite a while now. There's an insane amount of fan-fic out there, and most of it is garbage. This is where AI gaming is going. It'll become a lot easier to make a game, but just like writing doesn't make you an author, AI prompting doesn't make you a game dev. The result looks like that on first glance - a story on the one hand, something playable on the other - but close inspection will still reveal if someone actually knew what they were doing.

comments.author: Total_Engineering_51
comments.body:
For a certain part of the population this could be enough(the types that just play Madden/FC/CoD) as the small delta between variants allows for AI to fill in the blanks well enough. You want game x but reskinned with your favorite anime? Sure, the delta is small and the game is fundamentally unchanged. If you already loved game x, you’ll probably love the anime skinned version of it as well. This assumes the AI is accurately recreating the underlying data that drives the original game, not just making a shallow copy, something currently unproven… but for the sake of the discussion that’s accepted.  
The rub around this is the same argument that pops up with every other AI discussion around it being a tool versus the product owner(it makes all the critical choices): AI is bad at actually making things that are fundamentally new and interesting. Even just moving from reskin x with y theme to genre mixing, AI loses its useful roadmap and basically falls apart. Full game design means making tens of thousands of small decisions about how things work, even when just taking a novel approach to how two genres are smashed up. And sure, AI can make those decisions but did it make them well? The current models are leagues away from that and will likely always fall short on the taste and creativity scale. You can also sit down and work with it after the initial output, refining it to better suit your vision but after a few rounds of testing and changing things like that, the process just becomes game design by a different means, and most people aren’t going to want to “play” their AI generated game that way.
